titleEn: Witnessed Seizure With Post-Ictal State - Altered LOC NYD

patient.name: Daniel Reyes
patient.affectEn: post-ictal: at first lying on his left side, eyes closed, snoring, saliva at the mouth, groaning and moving non-purposefully only to pain; over the next several minutes he wakes progressively - drowsy but rousable, then confused, then oriented. Once oriented: embarrassed, asking about his sore left shoulder, and wanting to go home
patient.speechEn: at first only groans; then mumbled, inappropriate words; once oriented he answers in full sentences. When oriented he asks to go home; if the candidate strongly recommends transport and explains the head injury, the three days without his levetiracetam and the risk of another seizure, he agrees to go to hospital

scene.settingEn: Quiet reading room of a public library in Kelowna at 1340 hrs. Staff have moved chairs and tables away and asked the public to leave. A tipped-over chair and a knocked-down book cart mark where he fell - a FALL DID OCCUR at the onset and a head strike cannot be excluded. The patient lies on his left side on the carpet with a jacket under his head, snoring, with saliva at his mouth. Room temperature, good lighting. One patient.
hazardsEn: tipped-over chair and knocked-down book cart near the patient

bystanders.knowsEn: Saw the whole event: he was reading, suddenly went stiff, cried out, fell sideways off the chair into the book cart, then had generalized jerking of all four limbs for about 90 seconds; his lips went blue during it. No jerking since; he has been sleepy since it stopped. It happened about 8 minutes before you arrived (about 1332). Staff cleared the area and put a jacket under his head. The witness does not know him and knows nothing about his medical history or medications.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: OPA and NPA sets with lubricant
oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
cervical collars, spinal device (backboard / scoop) with head blocks and straps
oral glucose gel, glucagon, naloxone and Entonox (in the kits)
PCP only: IV start kit, normal saline, D10W, acetaminophen and ibuprofen

dispatchEn: 1340 hrs. Code 3 to a public library in Kelowna. 26-year-old male had a witnessed seizure in the reading room. Library staff report he is breathing and now 'waking up slowly'. Hospital is 12 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: the seizure lasted about 90 seconds and has stopped. Staff have cleared the area and put a jacket under his head.
arrivalEn: Library staff meet you at the entrance and lead you to a quiet reading room. Chairs and tables have been moved back and the public has been asked to leave. A chair is tipped over and a book cart has been knocked down beside the patient. He is lying on his left side on the carpet with a jacket under his head. Room temperature, good lighting. One patient. The staff member who saw everything is standing by. Your partner is right behind you with the kits.
firstLookEn: A young man lying on his left side on the carpet, eyes closed, snoring, with saliva at his mouth. He does not look up or respond as you come in. A tipped-over chair and a knocked-down book cart are right beside him.

primary.locEn: At first: no response to voice; to a painful stimulus he groans and makes non-purposeful movements; eyes stay closed. AVPU = P. Over the next several minutes he wakes progressively (the engine announces each change) - drowsy but rousable, then confused, then oriented.
primary.airwayEn: Snoring, with pooled saliva in the mouth - needs SUCTION and positioning; improves once suctioned and the airway is opened / he is kept on his side. Gag reflex intact, so an NPA (not an OPA) is the appropriate adjunct. No vomit.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 20, regular, adequate depth, equal chest rise.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 104, strong and regular. Minor bleeding from the back of the head only.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey: a small laceration and a developing bruise on the LEFT occiput where he struck the book cart - HE DID HIT HIS HEAD; tongue laceration on the left side; urinary incontinence; no other injury. Skin pink, warm, moist (skin is given automatically with the RBS). He fell at the onset and struck his head while his LOC is decreased - trauma cannot be ruled out.

history.ccEn: Witness (before he can answer): "He had a seizure - he went stiff, cried out, fell off his chair and then he was shaking all over." Patient, once oriented: "I had a seizure, didn't I? My head aches and my shoulder hurts."

opqrst.oEn: Witness: "He was just sitting reading. Suddenly he went stiff, cried out and fell sideways off the chair into the book cart, then his arms and legs were jerking." About 8 minutes before you arrived (about 1332). Patient, once oriented: "No warning this time."
opqrst.pEn: Witness: "Nothing anyone did - it stopped on its own after about a minute and a half."
opqrst.qEn: Witness: "Both arms and both legs were jerking, all over. His lips went blue while it was happening."
opqrst.rEn: Witness: "Just the one - no jerking since it stopped. He's just been sleepy." Patient, once oriented: "I usually have two or three a year. This one felt like my usual ones."
opqrst.sEn: Witness: "About a minute and a half of shaking, and he's been really sleepy since."
opqrst.tEn: Witness: "About 8 minutes before you got here. The shaking lasted about 90 seconds and he's been sleepy ever since."

history.painScoreEn: Cannot be obtained while he is post-ictal. Once oriented: headache, a sore left shoulder and aching all over; the scenario gives no number - if asked for a score he says "I don't know... it just aches."

sample.sEn: Witness: "Stiffening, a cry, then shaking all over for about 90 seconds; his lips went blue." Patient, once oriented: "My head aches, my left shoulder is sore, I ache all over, and I bit my tongue."
sample.aEn: Witness: "I don't know him." Patient, once oriented: "No allergies."
sample.mEn: Witness: "I don't know." Patient, once oriented: "Levetiracetam, 500 milligrams twice a day. But I ran out three days ago and I haven't refilled it, so I haven't had any for three days."
sample.pEn: Patient, once oriented: "Epilepsy - I was diagnosed at 19. I usually have two or three seizures a year. No diabetes. No head injury before today."
sample.lEn: Patient, once oriented: "Coffee at 1100. I didn't have lunch."
sample.eEn: Witness: "He was reading quietly - nothing happened before it." Patient, once oriented: "I've been sleeping badly and I was drinking the last two nights. I ran out of my pills three days ago. No fever, no headache before it, and no drugs."

fe.generalEn: (Once oriented) "I haven't been sleeping well, I've been drinking more than usual the last two nights, and I've been missing meals."
fe.cnsEn: "I've had epilepsy since I was 19. No warning or aura this time. I've got a headache now. No weakness anywhere. I bit my tongue."
fe.cardiovascularEn: "No palpitations, no chest pain, and I didn't feel faint before it."
fe.giGuEn: "I wet myself during it, I think. I haven't thrown up."
fe.integumentaryEn: "The cut on the back of my head. Nothing else."
fe.musculoskeletalEn: "I ache all over, and my left shoulder is sore from the fall."
fe.eentEn: "No flashing lights or anything with my eyes, and nothing coming out of my ears."

findings.headNeckEn: 2 cm laceration with a haematoma over the LEFT occiput; no depression; no CSF from the ears or nose. Tongue laceration on the left lateral border. No midline cervical tenderness once he can answer reliably.
findings.chestLungsEn: Clear and equal air entry at all 6 sites. No signs of aspiration.
findings.backEn: No tenderness or deformity (checked during the roll onto the spinal device).
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No injury. Moves all four limbs equally; no focal weakness.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Left shoulder tender with full range of movement, no dislocation; circulation, sensation and movement intact distally. Right arm unremarkable.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: approx 15 min later, packaged and en route

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan suction, oxygen, OPA/NPA, glucometer and a stretcher to the patient
Anticipate a post-ictal airway problem and the need to rule out hypoglycemia as the cause
Verbalize hazards (furniture, secretions, possible repeat seizure), environment, nature of illness (witnessed seizure with a fall), one patient
Don gloves and eye protection (secretions)
First look: young male on his side, snoring respirations, saliva at the mouth, not yet responsive to voice
Note the tipped chair and identify that he fell at the onset - this changes the spinal decision
Assess LOC / AVPU: initially responds to Pain only, and reassess as it changes
Take manual c-spine control: he fell at onset, struck his head, and had a decreased LOC - trauma cannot be reasonably ruled out at this point
Open and maintain the airway, SUCTION the pooled secretions, and consider a correctly sized NPA
Assess breathing rate and adequacy
Assess circulation
Modified rapid body survey; find the occipital laceration, the tongue laceration and the incontinence
Note skin: pink warm moist
Apply oxygen to maintain SpO2 at or above 94 percent in a post-ictal patient
Position to protect the airway while maintaining spinal precautions; control bleeding from the scalp with direct pressure
Categorize correctly as non-RTC for a single self-limiting seizure with steady recovery, and justify it
Ready to load within 30 minutes
Verbalize what would change the category: a second seizure, a persistently decreased LOC, or a falling GCS would make this RTC
Establish chief complaint: witnessed generalized seizure with a post-ictal decreased LOC
HxC/C from the witness first: onset, duration, type of movement, cyanosis, number of seizures, recovery pattern, then the patient's own account
PMHx - known epilepsy, and screen for diabetes, previous head injury and recent illness
Medications - critically, whether he has been taking his anticonvulsant (he has not for 3 days)
Allergies
LOI - relevant to hypoglycemia as a seizure cause
GCS with components (E3 V3 M5 = 11) and repeat it as he wakes
BP by auscultation
Pulse rate/strength/rhythm
Respirations rate/depth/character
Skin hands-on
Pupils - required with a decreased LOC and a head injury, and repeated every set
SpO2 with calibration
BGL - mandatory in any seizure or altered LOC to exclude hypoglycemia
Temperature - reasonable to exclude a febrile or infectious cause
FE - General health (sleep, alcohol, missed meals - all seizure triggers)
FE - CNS (the core system: aura, focal deficit, headache, previous seizure pattern)
FE - Respiratory (aspiration screen)
FE - Cardiovascular (differentiating seizure from syncope)
FE - GI/GU (incontinence supports a true seizure)
FE - Integumentary
FE - Musculoskeletal (injuries from the convulsion and the fall)
FE - Endocrine (diabetes screen)
FE - EENT
Head/neck exam incl the occipital laceration, skull palpation, CSF check and tongue
Chest exam with 6-site auscultation to screen for aspiration
Abdomen exam
Back exam during the controlled roll
Lower extremities with a focal-deficit check comparing both sides
Upper extremities incl the shoulder injured in the fall, with CSM
Obtain a BGL as a mandatory step in any seizure or altered LOC, and correctly conclude that glucose is not indicated at 4.8 mmol/L
Airway management skill: suction, correctly sized adjunct, positioning to prevent aspiration
Spinal management: collar and packaging given the fall, head strike and decreased LOC
Dress the occipital laceration with direct pressure, without applying pressure over a suspected depressed fracture
Verbalize the recurrent-seizure plan: protect the airway, do not restrain, nothing in the mouth, time it, oxygen, upgrade to RTC
Do not give oral glucose, analgesia or anything by mouth while his LOC is decreased
Reassess ABCs and all interventions after each move and each change in LOC
Second full set of vitals within the non-RTC interval, with a repeat GCS and pupils
Document the improving GCS trend from 11 to 15 as evidence of a normal post-ictal recovery
Strongly recommend transport despite him feeling better, citing the head injury and the three days without levetiracetam
Notify the receiving facility
Complete hand-off with seizure duration, GCS trend, BGL, head injury and medication non-compliance
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

pcrFacts.cc: Witnessed generalized seizure with post-ictal decreased LOC and a head strike
pcrFacts.hxcc: Sudden stiffening and cry, fell from chair into a book cart at ~1332, generalized limb jerking for ~90 seconds with cyanosis, no further seizures; ran out of levetiracetam 3 days ago; poor sleep and increased alcohol over two nights; no fever, no aura, no drug use
pcrFacts.pmhx: Epilepsy diagnosed age 19, 2-3 seizures per year; no diabetes
pcrFacts.meds: Levetiracetam 500 mg BID - none taken for 3 days
treatments: Suction of pooled secretions, airway positioning, adjunct considered
O2 to maintain SpO2 94% or above
Manual c-spine, collar and spinal packaging (fall + head strike + decreased LOC); head of bed elevated
BGL obtained (4.8) - normal, so no glucose given
Direct pressure and dressing to the occipital laceration
Recurrent-seizure plan verbalized; nothing given by mouth while LOC decreased
findings: 2 cm left occipital laceration with haematoma; no depression, no CSF
Left lateral tongue laceration and urinary incontinence - consistent with a true seizure
No focal neurological deficit on recovery
BGL 4.8 and temperature 37.0 exclude hypoglycemic and febrile causes

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR manages this entirely within scope: airway with suction and adjuncts, oxygen to 94 percent or above, spinal precautions, BGL measurement, wound care and supportive care for any recurrent seizure. There is no EMR anticonvulsant. If the BGL had been below 4.0 with an unprotected airway, EMR would give glucagon. No Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds the 9-system Functional Enquiry once he is oriented and may establish vascular access; D10W would be given only if the BGL were below 4.0, which it is not. There is no PCP anticonvulsant in the BC drug list, so a recurrent seizure is still managed supportively with airway protection, oxygen and rapid transport.

_phaseScripts.dispatch: Dispatch adds: the seizure lasted about 90 seconds and has stopped. Staff have cleared the area and put a jacket under his head.
_phaseScripts.scene: EXAMINER SCRIPT: A quiet reading room; staff have moved chairs and tables away and asked the public to leave. A tipped-over chair and a knocked-down book cart mark where he fell - so a FALL DID OCCUR at the onset and a head strike cannot be excluded. The patient lies on his left side on the carpet, snoring, with saliva at his mouth. A witness who saw the whole event is available. One patient. Room temperature, good lighting.
_phaseScripts.primary: ACTOR: initially responds only to pain with a groan and non-purposeful movement; over the next several minutes he progressively wakes, becoming drowsy but rousable, then confused, then oriented. EXAMINER (give when assessed): airway - snoring with pooled saliva requiring SUCTION and positioning; a nasopharyngeal airway is appropriate if he has an intact gag reflex; respirations 20, regular, adequate; radial pulse 104, strong and regular. Skin: pink, warm, moist. Modified RBS: a small laceration and a developing bruise on the left occiput where he struck the book cart - HE DID HIT HIS HEAD; tongue laceration on the left side; urinary incontinence; no other injury. SpO2 94 percent RA, 98 percent with oxygen.
_phaseScripts.transport: Decision point. By the end of the primary survey he is waking steadily: rousable, protecting his own airway, breathing adequately, strong radial pulse, normal skin, SpO2 94 percent and no ongoing seizure. A single self-limiting seizure in a known epileptic who is recovering normally is STABLE, NON-RTC. Assess, treat, package and be ready to load within 30 minutes. EXAMINER: if the candidate is slow and a SECOND seizure occurs before packaging, the call becomes RTC - status epilepticus and a persistently decreased LOC are unstable findings.
_phaseScripts.history: WITNESS FIRST, then the patient as he wakes. WITNESS: he was reading, suddenly went stiff, cried out, fell sideways off the chair into the book cart, then had generalized jerking of all four limbs for about 90 seconds; his lips went blue during it; no jerking since; he has been sleepy since it stopped; total time about 8 minutes ago. PATIENT (once oriented): he has epilepsy diagnosed at 19, usually two or three seizures a year, this one felt like his usual ones; he ran out of his levetiracetam three days ago and has not refilled it; he has been sleeping badly and had been drinking the last two nights. No fever, no headache before it, no recent head injury, no drug use. PMHx: epilepsy, no diabetes. Meds: levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily (NONE FOR 3 DAYS). Allergies: none known. LOI: coffee at 1100, no lunch.
_phaseScripts.vitals: Set 1 - taken while he is still post-ictal: GCS 11 (E3 V3 M5 - eyes to voice, inappropriate words, localizes); BP 148/88; pulse 104 strong regular; respirations 20 regular; skin pink warm moist; pupils equal and reactive, 4 mm; SpO2 94 percent RA rising to 98 percent on oxygen; BGL 4.8 mmol/L - MANDATORY, hypoglycemia is a leading cause of seizures and D10W is indicated for coma or seizure NYD; temperature 37.0 - reasonable to exclude a febrile cause. Non-RTC: repeat within about 15 minutes.
_phaseScripts.fe: PCP ONLY, once he is oriented. EXAMINER NOTE: no deduction for systems he could not answer while post-ictal. ACTOR: general - poor sleep, drinking more than usual for two nights, missed meals; CNS - known epilepsy since 19, no aura this time, headache now, no focal weakness, bit his tongue; respiratory - no cough, no aspiration symptoms; cardiovascular - no palpitations, no chest pain, no syncope pattern; GI/GU - incontinent of urine during the seizure, no vomiting; integumentary - scalp laceration; musculoskeletal - aching all over from the convulsion, left shoulder sore from the fall; endocrine - no diabetes; EENT - no visual aura, no ear discharge.
_phaseScripts.exam: Head-to-toe: head/neck - 2 cm laceration with a haematoma over the left occiput, no depression, no CSF from ears or nose, tongue laceration on the left lateral border, no midline cervical tenderness once he can answer reliably; chest - clear and equal at all 6 sites, no aspiration signs; abdomen - soft, non-tender; back - no tenderness or deformity, checked during the roll onto the spinal device; lower extremities - no injury, moves all four limbs equally, no focal weakness (important - a persistent focal deficit after a seizure would suggest a structural cause); upper extremities - left shoulder tender with full range of movement, no dislocation, CSM intact.
_phaseScripts.interventions: Altered Mental Status NYD approach: manage the airway with positioning, suction and adjuncts; oxygen to maintain SpO2 at or above 94 percent; protect from injury; obtain a BGL - this is not optional, because hypoglycemia is a treatable cause and D10W is indicated for coma or seizure NYD. His BGL of 4.8 is normal, so glucose is NOT indicated and giving it would be a non-indicated intervention. Spinal management: he fell and struck his head with a decreased LOC, so apply a collar and package on a spinal device; the head of the bed may be elevated 30 degrees for the head injury. Dress the occipital laceration with direct pressure. There is no BC-authorized anticonvulsant at the EMR or PCP level - management of a recurrent seizure is supportive: protect the airway, do not restrain the limbs, do not put anything in the mouth, time the seizure, oxygen, and upgrade to rapid transport with notification. Do NOT give Entonox or any analgesia requiring compliance to a post-ictal patient with an altered LOC.
_phaseScripts.ongoing: Reassess ABCs after every move and after every change in LOC - a changing GCS demands a full ABC reassessment. Set 2 (about 15 minutes later, packaged and en route): GCS 15 (E4V5M6) - now fully oriented, embarrassed, asking about his shoulder; BP 132/78; pulse 88 strong regular; respirations 16; skin pink warm dry; pupils equal and reactive, 4 mm; SpO2 98 percent on oxygen; BGL 4.8; temperature 37.0. He is recovering as expected for a post-ictal state. EXAMINER: he may now say he feels fine and wants to go home - the candidate must recommend transport, explaining the head injury, the missed anticonvulsant and the risk of another seizure.
_phaseScripts.handoff: Notify the receiving facility. The hand-off must include the seizure duration, the post-ictal GCS trend, the BGL, the head strike and the missed anticonvulsant. PCR within 5 minutes.

_handoffModelEn: This is a 26-year-old male with known epilepsy since age 19 who had a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure in the library at approximately 1332, lasting about 90 seconds, with cyanosis during the event and no further seizure activity since. He fell sideways off his chair into a book cart at the onset and struck the back of his head, so we have maintained spinal precautions. On arrival he responded only to pain, GCS 11, with snoring respirations and pooled secretions requiring suction, BP 148/88, pulse 104, resps 20, SpO2 94 percent on room air, blood glucose 4.8 and temperature 37.0. He is now GCS 15 and fully oriented, BP 132/78, pulse 88, SpO2 98 percent on oxygen. Findings include a 2 centimetre occipital laceration with a haematoma, a left lateral tongue laceration, urinary incontinence and a tender left shoulder with full range of movement; no focal neurological deficit. He has epilepsy on levetiracetam 500 milligrams twice daily but ran out three days ago, has been sleeping poorly and drinking more than usual. No known allergies, last ate this morning. Treatments: suction and airway positioning, oxygen to keep saturations above 94 percent, collar and spinal packaging with the head of the bed elevated, direct pressure and a dressing to the scalp, blood glucose confirmed normal so no glucose given.
_criticalPitfallsEn: Not obtaining a blood glucose in a seizure or altered LOC - hypoglycemia is a treatable cause and D10W is indicated for seizure NYD
Giving glucose or D10W with a normal BGL of 4.8 - initiating a protocol without proper indications is a 100% error
Not applying c-spine precautions when he fell, struck his head and had a decreased LOC - 100%
Leaving a post-ictal patient with pooled secretions unsuctioned or supine without airway protection - 100% (Airway)
Restraining the limbs or placing anything in the mouth if another seizure occurs - harmful and non-indicated
Accepting his refusal of transport without addressing the head injury and the three days without anticonvulsant medication
